My grandma had a great solution to Easter egg hunts. Since I am one of 13 grandkids it was a massive undertaking to fill up that many eggs, so she got creative. We had nickel hunts. She'd get like $50 worth of nickels from the bank and she'd scatter them all around the yard outside, as well as hide some on the porch, in planters, really obscure places.

After dinner we'd get to go on the hunt and each had a Ziploc bags to collect our nickels. Sometimes she'd even put some on the steps of the church across the street. Kept us busy for a few hours and out of our parents hair (we were old enough to not run off and the older cousins kept an eye on the younger cousins under like, 8)

Then we'd count our nickels and whoever found the most won a small prize, and the least one a small consultation prize. We'd count them all to see how many we'd missed. Usually never more than 10 were still out there each year. Plus we got to keep the nickels so we each would end up with like $5 worth, which is 100 nickels.

Sometimes we'd find ones from years past that were somewhat buried. My cousin Charlie broke out a metal detector one year and found like 8.

It was super fun, super easy to do, and got us outside and exercising while our parents got to chat.

My grandpa and grandma are gone now, and my mom and her siblings ended up selling the house. We told the buyer that they'll likely find some nickels on the property, and why they're there. He thought it was very sweet. We were very happy to find a buyer who wasn't going to tear the house down, as it's over 100 years old and is gorgeous. Also the squirrels my grandma liked to feed planted flowers in her garden when she died. They stole some tulip bulbs from the neighbors and buried them in front of my grandparents house. It was really sweet.
